key_insight: The paper builds neural network output classes that are inherently compatible with the PDE function spaces H(div) and H(curl), so the network always produces physically admissible vector fields while preserving jump discontinuities via de Rham operators.
engineering_relevance: This gives a mesh-free way to solve PDEs with discontinuous coefficients, interface jumps, curl-curl systems, transport, and conservation laws using a least-squares loss formulated in the natural weak spaces.
method: Map scalar/componentwise neural nets through fixed de Rham operators to create native H(div) and H(curl) classes.
Use skew-symmetric or scalar potentials to carry all interface jumps, while the remainder stays H^1-regular.
Train with a first-order system least-squares functional that matches the weak formulation and supports discontinuous solutions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical construction and problem instances rather than benchmark datasets, emphasizing space conformity and equivalence of the least-squares functional to the error for elliptic cases.
watch_item: Performance depends on knowing or learning interface geometry well; if jump locations are poorly represented, the potential-based decomposition may be harder to train reliably.
paper_title: FOSLS-deRhaNN: native de Rham neural classes for H(div) and H(curl) with applications to first-order system least-squares neural network methods for partial differential equations
